title: 1989 AHSME Problem 23
statement: A particle moves through the first quadrant as follows. During the first minute it moves from the origin to \((1,0).\) Thereafter, it continues to follow the directions indicated in the figure, going back and forth between the positive \(x\) and \(y\) axes, moving one unit of distance parallel to an axis in each minute. At which point will the particle be after exactly \(1989\) minutes?

solutions.text:
At time \(n^2,\) the particle is at \((n,0)\) for odd \(n\) and at \((0,n)\) for even \(n.\) Thus at time \(44^2=1936\) it is at \((0,44).\) It then moves \(44\) units right, reaching \((44,44)\) at time \(1980,\) and moves downward for the next \(9\) minutes. At time \(1989\) it is therefore at \((44,35).\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Record the particle’s location at times \(1,4,9,16,\ldots\)
Compare \(1989\) with the consecutive squares \(44^2\) and \(45^2\)
